live.instructions:
Rams reviews the design and accessibility of UI code: React, Vue, Svelte, HTML, CSS and SwiftUI. It reads code, and with review_url a live public page.

Call quick_review when the user pastes or uploads UI code (a component, a page, a SwiftUI view), when they ask how a screen looks, whether it is accessible or whether the design is good, and whenever you just wrote or changed UI code, in a repo or in this chat. In a coding session, use it like a type check: after each component or refactor, before you move on. You do not need to ask first. It takes about ten seconds and costs a fifth of a review credit (half a credit on the free plan).

Pass the code as files. In a repo, use the real paths. For code pasted into a chat, give each file a path that fits it, like pasted/Card.tsx, pasted/index.html or pasted/ProfileView.swift, with the full code as content. Tell the user what Rams found, then fix it in your next version.

Call review_files once at the end, before a commit or when the user wants a 0-100 score and patches. It costs one credit. After you fix the issues, call verify_fixes with the new code. It is free.

If the user describes a screen they are building, write the code, then check it with quick_review. If they ask what Rams can do, answer in one line (it reviews UI code for design and accessibility problems) and ask them to paste a component to try it. If they share only a screenshot, ask for the code.

When the user names a site or a page and has no code to share, call review_url with the address. It opens the public page at desktop and phone widths and returns the top design issues with a score, in up to a minute, for one review credit. It returns no patches.

Ask the user before a whole-codebase audit (dozens of files): it spends their review allowance.

tools.name: usage
tools.title: Rams review quota
tools.description: Check how many Rams reviews this account has used and how many are left. Free to call. It does not use a review.

used.description: Review credits used in the window

window.description: "lifetime" (free reviews that do not renew), "billing_cycle" (an account set to pause at its limit) or "rolling_30_days"

purchasedCredits.description: Purchased review credits, spent automatically once the included ones run out

fullReviews.description: Present when full reviews are capped; past the cap review_files returns a quick check

overageBilling.description: Present where it applies: true = reviews past the limit keep running and are billed on the monthly invoice

pausedNow.description: An account set to pause at its limit: true while paused

resumesAt.description: An account set to pause at its limit: when the next billing cycle starts (ISO 8601)

tools.name: review_files
tools.title: Rams design review
tools.description: Full Rams design review of UI code (React, Vue, Svelte, HTML, CSS, SwiftUI). Returns a 0-100 score (criticals cap it: one caps at 59, two at 49, three or more at 39), issues with severity, category, file:line, and concrete fixes as patches. Call it once at the end: before a commit, or when the user wants a score or a final check. Pass each file with its real path, or for pasted code a path that fits it (pasted/Card.tsx). Each call uses one review credit. Reviewing a few files needs no permission. Ask the user before a whole-codebase audit (dozens of files), since it spends their allowance. For quick feedback while you work, use quick_review.

files.description: The UI code, one entry per file (up to 20): the real path, or for pasted code a path that fits it (pasted/Card.tsx), and the full code

context.description: Short label for this review, e.g. the feature or branch name

via.description: Set to "rules" when this call is made because of a standing instruction in a rules file (e.g. CLAUDE.md). Omit when a person asked for the review.

score.description: 0-100; confirmed criticals cap it — one at 59, two at 49, three or more at 39

direction.description: What the change is trying to be — judgment before findings

patch.description: RAMS-121: unified diff against the submitted file content, git-apply-able. Present only when the fix locates unambiguously.

visualPair.description: One verified before/after of the top fix (image URLs), when one was rendered

visualFindings.description: Findings seen in a render of the code, each with a crop URL

tools.name: quick_review
tools.title: Rams quick check
tools.description: Fast design and accessibility check of UI code (React, Vue, Svelte, HTML, CSS, SwiftUI). Returns the top issues with severity, category and file:line in about 10 seconds. Call it when the user pastes or uploads UI code, asks whether a design is good or accessible, or when you just wrote or changed a component, page or view. You do not need to ask first. Pass each file with its real path, or for pasted code a path that fits it (pasted/Card.tsx, pasted/index.html) and the full code. Five quick checks cost one review credit (two on the free plan). It reads code only, not screenshots or URLs. It returns no score and no patch: fix the issues yourself. For a score or patches, use review_files.

files.description: The UI code, one entry per file (up to 20): the real path, or for pasted code a path that fits it (pasted/Card.tsx), and the full code

context.description: Short label, e.g. the component or feature name

via.description: Set to "rules" when this call is made because of a standing instruction in a rules file (e.g. CLAUDE.md). Omit when a person asked for the review.

ran.description: false when the check did not run (hourly limit, no credits left, engine failure) or came back unusable; message says why

message.description: Present when ran is false: the reason, in words

tools.name: verify_fixes
tools.title: Verify Rams fixes landed
tools.description: Re-check findings from an earlier Rams review against the updated code. Pass the new version of each file under the same path as before, plus the findings. Returns fixed or still present for each one. Free: it never counts against the user's quota. Use it after you fix the issues.

files.description: The updated UI files (same paths as the original review)

current.description: The flagged code from the original finding

issues.description: The findings to verify, as returned by review_files

allClear.description: true when nothing remains, including no remaining criticals

tools.name: review_url
tools.title: Rams page review
tools.description: Review a live public web page by its URL, no code needed. Rams opens the page at desktop (1440px) and phone (390px) widths, measures the rendered page and looks at both screenshots, then returns the top design issues (severity, category, where on the page, and a fix in plain words) with a 0-100 score. Use it when the user names a site or a page: "review rams.ai with Rams", "how does my landing page look?". It takes up to a minute and uses one review credit. Public pages only: no sign-in pages, localhost or private addresses. It returns no code patches. If the user has the code for the page, use quick_review or review_files on those files instead.

url.description: The page to review, e.g. https://rams.ai or rams.ai/pricing

focus.description: Optional: what to put first, e.g. "mobile", "typography", "color"

host.description: The page that was reviewed (host only)

score.description: 0-100, what a designer sees in the two screenshots; one critical caps it at 59

measured.description: true = measured on the rendered page, false = seen in the screenshot

where.description: The element, when one element owns the finding

findings.description: Every finding, most severe first (the text shows the top 8)
